title: Fix SSE streaming chunking/framing: partial JSON reassembly, delimiter and token ordering
author: Ava Chen
description: Motivation: Streaming SSE responses occasionally produced malformed or out-of-order events in the OpenAI-compat and native SSE endpoints. Root causes: a) partial JSON objects split across TCP/SSE chunk boundaries were emitted as separate events, leading consumers that expect a single JSON payload per 'data:' event to fail JSON.parse; b) delimiter handling could emit empty events when CRLF boundaries aligned poorly; c) token/event ordering race where batching/flush hooks interleaved partial tokens (particularly when tool/function-calling structured outputs were enabled). This PR reworks the SSE framer and the OpenAI-compat streaming adapter to buffer and reassemble partial payloads, enforce explicit event framing, and attach stable sequence indices to each logical token/event so downstream clients can reconstruct ordered streams even in the face of transport-level reordering. Changes include: buffering+reassembly with size/safety guards, atomic emission of structured-output tokens to avoid splitting JSON objects across events, deterministic index fields in openai-compat deltas, and added integration/unit tests that simulate abrupt socket closes and boundary-split tokens. The description below contains commit summary, changed files, test/CI notes, and a short rollout plan.
commits: a1f3b2c: refactor sse framer to expose buffer/reassembly primitives
b2d4e8f: implement partial-payload assembler and size guard (max_partial_payload=64KB)
c3e6f1a: openai_compat: add delta.index and atomic delta emission for structured outputs
d4f7a2b: add integration tests for boundary-split SSE events and abrupt connection close
e5a8c3d: fix race in flush routine; add lock around framer flush path
f6b9d4e: docs: add note to streaming troubleshooting and release notes
review_comments: Diego Morales (reviewer): Found a race where _flush_locked could run concurrently with assemble_partial; recommended adding an explicit lock and a max-buffer-size guard to avoid unbounded memory growth. Also asked for explicit CI tests that simulate socket chunking at different offsets.

Ava Chen (author): Addressed by adding ReentrantFramerLock and max_partial_payload default to 65536 bytes; added integration test that simulates chunk splits at offsets 1..64 on representative payloads.

Priya Nair (reviewer): Noted that openai_compat previously emitted incremental 'delta' events without a stable index which made replay/reassembly hard for clients. Suggested adding index on each delta and keeping consistent ordering guarantees. Also asked to ensure function/tool-calling structured JSON is emitted atomically.

Ava Chen (author): Added delta.index and delta.is_atomic flags; modified framer to buffer structured JSON tokens and emit them in a single 'data:' event. Added unit tests asserting that atomic structured outputs are parsable by json.loads once per event.

Evan Brooks (reviewer): Suggested adding observability counters for partial_reassembly_hits, partial_reassembly_errors, and atomic_emit_count. Also requested a note in docs explaining the safety limits and failure modes.
Ava Chen (author): Added metrics and docs section; CI coverage expanded to include simulated high-throughput streaming scenario.
release_notes: Fix SSE streaming framing bugs: reassemble partial JSON payloads across chunk boundaries, prevent delimiter-induced empty events, ensure token/event ordering and atomic emission for structured tool/function-calling outputs. Adds observability counters for streaming reassembly and safety guards against oversized partial payloads.
testing_notes: Added deterministic tests that split payloads at byte offsets and assert single-event JSON parseability. Integration test simulates abrupt connection close and verifies no partial JSON is emitted to consumers. CI expanded with streaming stress test that validates metrics for reassembly/error conditions.
rollout_plan: Deploy to canary (perf-canary) for 24h with streaming telemetry enabled; monitor partial_reassembly_errors and streaming_latency; if stable, roll to release branch and cut patch release. If regressions observed, revert via feature flag that toggles atomic emission in framer.
notes: This PR touches the OpenAI compatibility layer to preserve compatibility with clients that assume one JSON object per 'data:' event (delta style). It also prevents regressions where structured outputs (function/tool calls) were accidentally split across events and caused downstream parsers to error. Performance impact is minimal thanks to small buffer sizes and short-circuit when payload is already complete.
